Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz on order

Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1646–1716) approaches order within Rationalism. He described reality as coordinated monads, defended sufficient reason and the best possible world, and independently developed calculus. Systematically, the teaching links metaphysics, logic, calculus into a practical and theoretical whole. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets order most directly—useful for searches such as “gottfried wilhelm leibniz quotes on order.”
